key_insight: An energy-structure-preserving finite element scheme provides mesh-independent stability for three-dimensional rotating MHD-Boussinesq flows with nonlinear power-law viscosity.
engineering_relevance: The method supports stable simulation of rotating, electrically conducting fluids with thermal coupling and shear-dependent viscosity.
method: Conforming velocity and temperature elements, Nédélec magnetic elements, and semi-implicit backward Euler time stepping.
Exact Lorentz–induction energy cancellation and energy-neutral Coriolis forces.
Time-translate compactness and a Minty argument for nonlinear diffusion.
evidence_signal: Three-dimensional numerical experiments confirm the predicted stability and convergence behaviour, alongside a priori error estimates requiring no mesh–time coupling.
watch_item: Weak-solution identification is established for Newtonian viscosity and, in 3D, above a Lorentz-force-driven power-law threshold—not throughout the full shear-thickening regime.
paper_title: Finite Element Approximation of Rotating MHD-Boussinesq Flows with Nonlinear Power-Law Viscosity
